items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: Oh, Gilles Rouge, the piccolo player? Yeah. Gilles Rouge was about then, well, I'd say about 18.

ctx.x: You was older than any of the other fellas.
Were you older than Gilles Rouge? The old musicians? No. No. Who was older than you? They were older than me. Who? Braun and Secrets and all them guys. They were older than me.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: One piccolo player. And we had clarinet... Oh, Gilles Rouge, the piccolo player? Yeah... Gilles Rouge was about then, well, I'd say about 18.

ctx.x: Let's see, what kind of instruments did y'all have for that? Just drums and piccolos? Yes, we had one piccolo. One piccolo.
One piccolo player. And we had clarinet. Clarinet. Trombone. Trombone. Carnet. Alto. Tuba. Tuba. And baritone. Of course, drums, of course. And one piccolo.

One piccolo. Now that again was when you were 15 years old. That was around 15 years old. Yeah. I'll be there. Yes. Mm-hmm. Yes. And none of your music had any name to it. You didn't play any, you didn't know the name of any of the songs you played? Never knew the name. The whole thing was just out of your head.
